web_evidence.title: Prep by Curtis Sittenfeld | Excerpt
web_evidence.note: A sustained opening-chapter excerpt, reprinted with permission from Random House Trade Paperbacks, presents Lee as the participating narrating I throughout scene action and reflection.

web_evidence.title: Between Meritocracy and the Old Boy Network: Elite Education in Contemporary American Literature
web_evidence.note: Sophie Spieler’s scholarly analysis explicitly identifies Lee as a first-person narrator chronicling all four Ault years and as the novel's controlling narrator and focalizer.

web_evidence.title: Novelist Sittenfeld chronicles 'Prep' life
web_evidence.note: In an interview, Sittenfeld explicitly contrasts her next novel's third-person narration with Prep's first-person narration and describes Prep as covering Lee's four school years.

web_evidence.title: A moment with ... Curtis Sittenfeld, novelist
web_evidence.note: The contemporary newspaper profile describes Prep as tracking its first-person narrator through four years and identifies Lee Fiora as that narrator.

search_log: Searched "Curtis Sittenfeld Prep excerpt first chapter publisher" and opened the permission-authorized Bookreporter opening excerpt plus Penguin Random House's title and reader-guide pages.
Searched "Curtis Sittenfeld Prep novel first person narrator Lee Fiora point of view" and opened explicit POV descriptions; weaker study-guide and user-review results were not needed as evidence.
Searched for scholarly analysis of Prep's narrator and opened the COPAS article, which explicitly describes Lee's first-person narration across all four years.

Searched author interviews and reputable contemporary coverage for possible frame or person changes; the Daily Princetonian and Seattle Post-Intelligencer sources corroborated first person, and no sustained third-person or second-person sections were found.
person_note: The quote set repeatedly exposes Lee as a participating retrospective narrator through sustained I, me, my, and occasional inclusive we narration across school scenes and later-life reflection. Generalized you passages are rhetorical or gnomic rather than a separate second-person strand, while first-person language confined to quoted dialogue is non-base. The authorized opening excerpt independently shows the same controlling first-person voice, and scholarly whole-book analysis explicitly states that Lee chronicles all four Ault years as the first-person narrator. Contemporary author-interview and newspaper evidence corroborate that structure. No credible evidence of an alternating frame or another controlling person was found; the only minor uncertainty is that the authorized prose excerpt covers the opening rather than every chapter, which the whole-book structural sources resolve.
